result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by wide sidewalks but lacks protective features like street trees or buffers. A significant conflict point exists on the left where a large parking garage entrance crosses the walkway, while the right side is bordered by an open surface parking lot.

hazards.name: Wide Driveway Curb Cut
hazards.description: A large entrance to a parking garage on the left creates a wide conflict zone where vehicles cross the pedestrian path.
hazards.location_in_image: Left foreground, entrance to the white multi-story garage

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: There is no physical separation or planting strip between the sidewalk and the moving traffic lanes.

interventions.title: Driveway Narrowing
interventions.description: Reduce the width of the garage entrance and use high-visibility pavement markings to alert drivers to the pedestrian zone.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Planters
interventions.description: Install a furniture zone with trees or planters to provide a physical buffer and improve the pedestrian experience.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at the nearest intersection to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility.

result.summary: The environment features a wide roadway with a marked crosswalk and a paved sidewalk separated from a large surface parking lot. While a walkway exists, the presence of a large drainage grate and multiple vehicle conflict points from the adjacent parking lot reduces pedestrian comfort and safety.

hazards.name: Large drainage grate
hazards.description: A wide metal grate runs parallel to the sidewalk, potentially creating a tripping hazard or difficulty for small wheels like strollers or wheelchairs.
hazards.location_in_image: Between the roadway and the sidewalk in the mid-ground.

hazards.name: Parking lot conflict points
hazards.description: The large surface parking lot creates points where vehicles cross the pedestrian path, increasing the risk of collisions.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image where the sidewalk meets the parking lot entrance.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at the crosswalk to reduce crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Upgrade the existing crosswalk markings to a high-visibility continental pattern to increase driver awareness.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features continuous, wide sidewalks on both sides of a two-lane urban street. While sidewalks are in good condition, the streetscape is characterized by large-scale buildings with relatively blank frontages and some temporary obstructions on the walkway.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: Construction barrels and cones on the left sidewalk partially block the pedestrian path.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the image, on the sidewalk near the red car.

hazards.name: Blank Frontage
hazards.description: The presence of long, windowless walls and parking garage openings reduces natural surveillance and creates a less inviting pedestrian environment.
hazards.location_in_image: Buildings on both sides of the street.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at the intersection to shorten crossing distances and improve pedestrian visibility.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Planters
interventions.description: Add a furniture zone with trees or planters to create a more inviting environment and provide a consistent buffer between pedestrians and vehicles.

result.summary: The image shows a wide, well-maintained sidewalk adjacent to a large parking garage with a blank brick facade. A gated vehicle entrance creates a potential conflict point for pedestrians, and the lack of a buffer or street-level activity makes the environment feel sterile.

hazards.name: Vehicle Conflict Point
hazards.description: A gated entrance to a parking garage crosses the sidewalk, creating a risk of collision between pedestrians and exiting/entering vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Center, gated opening in the building wall.

hazards.name: Blank Frontage
hazards.description: The long, windowless brick wall provides no 'eyes on the street', reducing perceived safety and pedestrian comfort.
hazards.location_in_image: Left and right sides of the building facade.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Buffer
interventions.description: Install a planting strip or street trees between the sidewalk and the roadway to provide physical and psychological separation from traffic.

interventions.title: Enhanced Driveway Markings
interventions.description: Use high-visibility pavement markings or a change in material across the garage entrance to alert drivers to the presence of pedestrians.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Add dedicated street lighting poles to improve visibility and safety for pedestrians during nighttime hours.
